text:
cassie: Hey folks — quick sync on the rate "slab" wording and the example snippet for the pricing page. I pushed a small PR but want to confirm header examples and the dashboard panel link before merge.

jules: Looking now. Are we changing 'tiers' -> 'slabs' throughout or just the pricing table?

cassie: Just the user-facing docs where we describe incremental pricing buckets: 'slabs' feels clearer than 'tiers' for metered increments. Back-end names stay the same.

priya: Fine from billing side as long as we add a short glossary line: "Slab = incremental usage bucket used to compute marginal per-unit price." Can we show a worked example?

cassie: Yep. Thinking a 3-slab example: 0-100k tokens @ $0.0008, 100k-1M @ $0.0006, >1M @ $0.00045. I'll add a compact table and a short worked calc.

ben: For SDK snippets, we should show both the response headers and the new client helper. Quick idea: curl headers + JS snippet.

jules: Suggest header names we actually return: X-Usage-Slab, X-Usage-Consumed, X-Billing-Rate. Current runtime returns X-Quota-Remaining and X-Rate-SlabId. Is that accurate, @tom?

tom: Runtime team: we return X-Quota-Remaining and X-Rate-Slab for now. We can add X-Billing-Rate but it's a small endpoint change. Prefer docs to use what's stable (X-Quota-Remaining, X-Rate-Slab) and show how to map to UI.

cassie: OK — docs will show the stable headers and a quick mapping table: header -> meaning -> how to use in UI.

priya: Also include note about eventual consistency for quota counters (some dashboards lag ~30s). Add a small callout.

cassie: Good call. I'll add a subtle warning box.

laura: One UX ask: change the dashboard panel name from "Quota overview" to "Billing by slab" so customers find it faster. Is that a config change or just docs?

tom: That's a dashboard rename in Grafana. I can rename but need a migration note so existing permalinks still work. I'll add a redirect link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/usage?panel=slab (new) -> old permalink will redirect for 90 days.

cassie: Perfect. Can we include the preview link for the docs PR for reviewers? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1599 — preview: https://deploy-preview-1599--docs.redwood.ai/rate-slabing (WIP)

ben: Sample snippets to include (inline):
```
# curl: show headers from API
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -d '{"model":"rwd/llama-3-small","input":"hello"}'
# look for headers: X-Quota-Remaining, X-Rate-Slab
```

ben: And a JS SDK example (v2):
```js
// v2 client returns headers via response.metadata
const res = await client.completions.create({model: 'rwd/llama-3-small', input: 'hi'});
console.log(res.metadata['x-quota-remaining']);
console.log(res.metadata['x-rate-slab']);
```

cassie: Nice. Add a brief migration note: in SDK v1 users read headers from the raw HTTP response; in v2 we expose them on res.metadata. Link to SDK migration guide.

jules: Nit: please format the pricing table so it uses monospace for token counts and an inline formula example. e.g., "Cost = 100k * $0.0008 + 900k * $0.0006" for the sample.

cassie: Will do. Also adding a one-line snippet for the dashboard alert rule we recommend: trigger when rolling 1h cost delta > $50.

priya: Add billing contacts and legal note about rounding (we bill to the cent daily). Small detail but customers ask.

cassie: All items listed: glossary, worked example, header mapping table, SDK curl+JS snippets, dashboard rename + redirect note, alert example, rounding/billing note. I'll update the PR tonight and tag reviewers.

deploy-bot: deploy-preview-1599 started — build 78 running (netlify). Preview URL: https://deploy-preview-1599--docs.redwood.ai/rate-slabing

laura: Thanks — i'll review content tomorrow and test the dashboard link. If everything looks good, we can merge after tom renames Grafana panel and confirms redirect.

cassie: Thanks everyone. I'll assign the PR to @laura and @jules for review and to @tom for the dashboard action. Tagging checklist in the PR description so nothing slips. :sparkles:

jules: LGTM for content structure. Quick follow-up: can we also add an example for embeddings metering? same slabs but per-embedding-unit calc.

cassie: Yes — adding a tiny embeddings worked example (1 embedding = 512 units for the calc). That should keep the page compact.

priya: Great. Thanks team.

cassie: Closing loop — will ping when PR is ready for final review.
